summary: The highest-risk paths are privileged legacy config/task routes, unauthenticated log streaming, raw shell startup, host Docker socket access, and destructive rollback without validation.
findings: backend/main.py exposes /api/config and many legacy task/provider routes with default-admin behavior through get_legacy_user().
backend/api/v2/websocket.py exposes task logs and status for any task id without auth or ownership checks.
backend/services/site_service.py executes start_command through sh -lc, which preserves shell injection semantics.
docker-compose.yml mounts /var/run/docker.sock into main-service and celery-worker by default.
backend/services/version_service.py removes the live site tree before validating restore success.
